title: Automated Batching/Caching Advisor with SLO-Enforced Rollouts
creator: Marta Alvarez
description: Build an automated advisor and safe-apply system that recommends batching and KV/prefix caching configurations per route and can apply them behind SLO-enforced guardrails. The goal is to reduce per-token cost while preserving p95/p99 latency SLOs for high-priority routes. The feature includes recommendation generation, a staged canary apply flow, SLO-aware routing fallbacks, limiters to prevent over-aggressive batching, and anomaly detection with automatic rollback triggers.
context: We currently have manual tuning guides and heuristics for batching and KV caching. Customers (and internal tenants) have requested an automated advisor that produces per-route configs and can safely apply them at scale. Previous experiments showed up to 28% token-cost reduction for long-sequence generative workloads but introduced tail-latency regressions for small synchronous routes when batching windows were too aggressive. This ticket operationalizes a safe rollout pattern and observability for automated applies.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces per-route recommendations (max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, prefix_cache_enabled, kv_cache_ttl) for 95% of active routes and surfaces confidence score
Canary apply framework can roll out recommendations to a configurable fraction of traffic (1%, 10%, 50%) and automatically pause if SLOs degrade
SLO guardrails prevent any apply from increasing p99 latency by >20ms or reducing throughput below configured target for the route
Anomaly detection detects regressions within 5 minutes of apply and triggers automated rollback and incident notification
End-to-end integration tests and canary runbook documented and validated on staging cluster
implementation_notes: Recommendation engine: batch stats aggregator pulls 7-day histograms of sequence length, inter-arrival times, and kv-hit ratios from metrics pipeline (Prometheus + ClickHouse) and scores configs by cost/latency trade-off
Limiters at apply-time: global token-per-second cap, per-route max_batch_size ceiling, per-tenant fairness weight to avoid noisy-neighbor batching monopolies
SLO-aware routing: requests tagged as 'latency-sensitive' are routed to a low-batching variant; non-latency-sensitive traffic can be routed to optimized variant via weighted routing policy
Anomaly detection: Alert rules (Prometheus) + ML-based drift detector (lightweight) watching p95/p99, error-rate, median-kv-latency; thresholds plumbed into rollout controller
Safe-apply controller: implements canary phases, monitors metrics, and supports automated rollback + manual override; exposes audit log entries and PR-style diff for applied config
Telemetry: record apply_id, recommendation_id, metrics baseline and post-apply windows, and execution trace for root-cause analysis
Testing harness: synthetic traffic generator to validate latency/throughput under different batching configs and KV cache cold-start scenarios
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): unit + integration tests, local presubmit check (jenkins/gha) - target branch feature/eng-9142
Stage 1 (staging canary): apply to 1% traffic for 24h with extended telemetry collection
Stage 2 (selected customers/internal): apply to 10% for 48h and run chaos tests (node restarts, slow disk)
Stage 3 (broader rollout): 50% then 100% with 2-hour observation gates and manual approvals for P0 routes
At each gate the safe-apply controller evaluates SLO objectives and runs anomaly detectors before progressing
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback if any of the following triggers fire within monitoring window: p99 increase > 20ms (absolute) OR p95 increase > 50ms OR throughput drop > 10% for the route OR error-rate increase > 0.5%
Manual rollback via console / API: recorded as revert with apply_id; revert produces a new audit entry and triggers a follow-up investigation ticket
Post-rollback: capture heap/profile + KV cache snapshot for root-cause; schedule regression test with smaller step sizes
If rollback occurs during canary, block similar recommendations for 24 hours and add route to 'guarded' list
monitoring_criteria: Primary SLOs: per-route p99 latency < configured SLO (route metadata) and throughput >= baseline * (1 - 0.05)
Secondary: token-cost per-1000-requests decreases by >= 8% for routes where recommendations applied
Detection latency: anomalies flagged within 5 minutes; alert escalations after 15 minutes if unresolved
Observability: dashboards show baseline vs current windows, apply diff, and per-tenant impact heatmap

notes: Trade-offs: Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases variance and cold-start risk. Default recommendations skew conservative for latency-sensitive routes and aggressive for background embeddings/async jobs.
Per-route metadata: we rely on a 'latency_priority' tag (0|1|2) set in the API catalog. Missing tags default to conservative behavior.
Security: configs are stored encrypted in customer-specific namespaces; no PII is included in recommendations. KMS integration covered under ENG-9075.
Open question: whether to expose a per-customer override API for customers on Dedicated; initial plan to allow 'opt-out' flag via account settings
